title: When the Hollow Wakes Again
premise: In the city of Vellamark, where magic was outlawed after the Sundering, Oscar Delacroix survives by hiding her beast-speaker gift behind cheap charms and careful silence. When the crown's new Inquisitor begins burning names off census rolls and hunting the gifted, Oscar is exposed by the very crows she once befriended, forcing her to flee into the wild hollows with a disgraced lawkeeper and a child who hears the dead. To end the hunt, she must seek the feral courts of beast and bone and reforge the broken covenant between human and wild realms, discovering that the old pact failed not from betrayal but from humanity's refusal to listen. The story ends with Oscar sacrificing her own voice to seal the new covenant, silencing her gift forever but waking the land itself as witness, so that no crown can ever again claim the wild belongs to them alone.
about_author: Wren Yarrow is the pen name of a former field naturalist who spent six years cataloguing birdsong in remote wetlands before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about the voices humans refuse to hear, drawing on folklore gathered from border villages where the old covenants were said to have been signed.

chapters.title: Charms for the Fearful
chapters.summary: Oscar Delacroix sells luck-knots and weather-whispers in the market of Vellamark, hiding her true gift beneath harmless trinkets. Through her POV we see her careful double life: feeding crows on the roof, trading secrets with a hedge-witch, never staying anywhere too long. When she heals a dying sparrow in public view, an old woman sees. Emotional beat: the fragile comfort of invisibility, and the first hairline crack in it.

chapters.title: The Census of Names
chapters.summary: The crown announces a registry of 'afflicted persons,' and Inquisitor Serane Halveth arrives with cold efficiency and a ledger. Oscar's POV: she watches neighbors denounce each other for small kindnesses to animals. Her hedge-witch friend Maren urges her to run; Oscar refuses, believing she can outlast the storm. Emotional beat: dread compounding into denial, the cost of believing rules will protect you.

chapters.title: What the Crows Remember
chapters.summary: The crows Oscar has fed for years are captured and compelled by Halveth's iron charms to betray the one who speaks their tongue. Oscar watches, hidden, as they scream her name and street. She burns her stall and flees at night with nothing but Maren's warning and a stolen map of the hollows. Emotional beat: betrayal that isn't betrayal—the animals had no choice—and grief sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Lawkeeper Who Fell
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Dain Corvel, a lawkeeper stripped of rank for refusing to hand over his gifted sister, now living rough in the border woods. He catches Oscar stealing from his snares but recognizes what she is—and chooses not to report her. Together they find Tam, an orphaned child who hears the dead speaking through roots and stones. Emotional beat: two wary strangers discovering that exile makes strange kinships.

chapters.title: Into the Hollow Country
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV as the three flee deeper into the wild hollows, where the land grows strange and watchful. Tam's gift reveals that the forest remembers the old covenant—a treaty sealed in blood and song between human kings and the feral courts, broken three years ago when the last speaker died. Something vast begins following them. Emotional beat: awe tangled with fear; the wild is neither kind nor cruel, only waiting.

chapters.title: The Court of Root and Antler
chapters.summary: Captured by the feral court, Oscar stands before the Stag Sovereign, who blames humanity for the covenant's breaking and the long winter now falling across both realms. She learns the truth: the pact requires a living speaker on each side, and the human side was left vacant. Halveth's hunters breach the court seeking her. Emotional beat: fury and recognition—Oscar realizes the crown's hunt and the wild's wrath are the same wound.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Ledger
chapters.summary: Dain's POV during a desperate escape: he holds the pass against Halveth's soldiers while Oscar and Tam flee, and is taken prisoner rather than killed—Halveth wants him as bait. Meanwhile Oscar, wounded, must decide whether to save him or reach the covenant-stone before the first snow seals it for another century. Emotional beat: the terrible arithmetic of loyalty; justice outside any law.

chapters.title: The Price of a Voice
chapters.summary: Oscar trades her greatest secret to the river-hags: the way into Vellamark's prison and the location of the buried covenant-stone beneath the old cathedral. She rescues Dain, learning Halveth herself carries a suppressed gift—the Inquisitor hates what she is. Oscar offers her a choice instead of a fight. Emotional beat: compassion as strategy; enemies revealed as mirrors.

chapters.title: When the Hollow Wakes
chapters.summary: Climax. At the covenant-stone, Oscar must speak for humanity—but a living voice must be given, not lent. As Halveth's forces and the feral host converge on the cathedral ruins, Oscar speaks the old words and gives up her gift entirely, pouring her beast-speech into the stone. The land wakes: every rooted thing, every creature becomes witness and party to the new covenant. Emotional beat: sacrifice transfigured into belonging.

chapters.title: A Quiet Tongue
chapters.summary: Resolution. Winter breaks early. Oscar, voiceless to beasts but fluent among people, opens a school in rebuilt Vellamark where gifted children learn openly; Tam becomes the first licensed speaker under the new covenant, and Halveth, pardoned, keeps the registry as a record of apology. On the last page, a crow lands on Oscar's windowsill, and though she cannot hear its words, she understands its meaning anyway. Emotional beat: peace earned, not granted; some bonds outlast the gifts that made them.
